capabilities: attach formulas to computed values in Markdown tables and prose anchors
recompute values and flag numbers that no longer agree with their formulas
mark computed values in reading mode and Live Preview
propose rules that reproduce the numbers a plain table already contains
disambiguation: Not a spreadsheet replacement — no grid, no Excel file compatibility; it checks numbers inside ordinary Markdown documents.
extras: The README documents the whole VisiMark project (CLI, MCP server, lint rules, editor plugins); the Obsidian plugin is one artifact, whose stated role is marking every computed value in reading mode and Live Preview. Not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The project began as a CSV-based idea and moved to Markdown so that several small sheets can live inside one master document and the file renders as a document rather than as data.
problem: Plain Markdown has no way to record that a number derives from other inputs, so when an input changes every downstream figure is a guess until a human re-checks it by hand.

relations.evidence: The name is a nod to VisiCalc

summary: Checks that every computed number in a note still matches the formula that produced it, and marks computed values in reading mode and Live Preview.
